stages.name: Short run and long run
stages.title: Short run and long run
stages.sub: After this you can say whether a business decision belongs to the short run or the long run.

steps.q: A bakery gets a rush of orders. Staff can be hired fast, but a new oven takes months. Can it add ovens this week?
steps.right: No, the ovens stay the same for now
steps.wrong: Yes, it can add ovens straight away
steps.hint: Think about what can be changed quickly and what cannot.

steps.q: In that same week, can the bakery still change how many workers it uses?
steps.right: Yes, staffing can be adjusted quickly
steps.hint: The bakery hired two more staff almost immediately. Could it do that with ovens?

steps.q: During this period, with ovens fixed but staff adjustable, what kind of time period is the bakery operating in?
steps.right: A period where at least one factor is fixed
steps.wrong: A period where every factor can change
steps.hint: You just found one factor that cannot change yet, and one that can.

steps.q: A year later, the bakery has built a new kitchen with extra ovens. Is anything still stuck at its old level?
steps.right: No, all factors can now be changed
steps.wrong: Yes, the ovens are still fixed
steps.hint: Enough time has passed to build new premises. What is left unchangeable?

steps.q: This week a furniture firm can add overtime but not workshop space; next year it could build another. What separates the two situations?
steps.right: Whether every factor of production can be varied
steps.wrong: Whether the firm makes a profit or a loss
steps.hint: Focus on what can and cannot be changed, not on money made.
